Notes on Rate Limiting

A token bucket is the right default for polite fetching because it permits a burst and then settles into a steady rate. That shape matches how servers actually experience load: a handful of requests arriving together is unremarkable, while a sustained stream from one client is what gets noticed and blocked.

The important parameter is not the rate but the scope. Limiting globally protects your own machine from doing too much work at once, and limits nothing that any individual server experiences. Limiting per host is what keeps you welcome, because a server only sees the traffic you send to it.

Honoring Retry-After is the other half. A server that tells you when to come back has given you the exact information you need, and ignoring it converts a temporary throttle into a permanent ban with remarkable efficiency.
